title: Its front was burned and melted in its owner's barracks during a bombing in the Gulf War.
description:
Its front was burned and melted in its owner's barracks during a bombing in the Gulf War. Its owner, Stephan Scoggins, a medic deployed in the war, posted it to Nintendo Power asking for a replacement.

Nintendo's technicians wrote it off, then found it still powered on. Start and Select still worked, so they tested it with Tetris. That is all the source confirms: not that every button and the screen survived.

printed his letter and sent him a new Game Boy 'as a special Desert Storm courtesy'

The scorched console went on show in Nintendo's New York store, switched on and playing Tetris. Keeping it running took new batteries and, at one point, a replacement screen.

In 2023 a store worker confirmed it had been quietly sent back to Nintendo of America's headquarters in Redmond, Washington. It is unclear whether it will ever go back on show.

Sources:
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_New_York: confirms the store's museum displayed a Game Boy owned by Dr Stephan Scoggins, a medic deployed in the Gulf War; that its front was burned and melted in his barracks during a bombing; that he sent it to Nintendo Power asking for a replacement; that technicians judged it a 'lost cause' but found it still powered on with Start and Select working, testing it with Tetris; that Nintendo Power sent him a replacement 'as a special Desert Storm courtesy' and ran his letter in issue 26 (July 1991); and that it was confirmed in 2023 to have been returned to Nintendo of America's headquarters in Redmond, Washington.
- https://www.siliconera.com/the-gulf-war-game-boy-says-goodbye-to-nintendo-new-york-store-removed/: confirms the removal was reported on 29 to 30 June 2023 after a store worker said it had gone back to Redmond, and that the unit on display had received a screen replacement and new batteries when needed.
